messages:
John (Acme): Hey team — since yesterday's deploy we're seeing intermittent invalid JSON responses from /v1/generate when using JSON mode. Broke prod flows. Example attached. request_id=rq_9a7b 

Maya - Support: Sorry to hear that, John. Can you paste the raw response you got and minimal repro steps? Also which model and SDK version?

John (Acme): here's the raw body we received (notice it's not valid JSON):
```
{"id":1,"result":{"name":"Alice"}}{"id":2,"result":{"name":"Bob"}}
```
This started after the March runtime deploy. We also saw a bunch of 500s and a latency spike.

Maya - Support: Thanks — that looks like outputs got concatenated. Are you using prefix/KV caching or batching? Any concurrent requests on the same conversation_id?

John (Acme): We're on redwood-14b-rl, SDK 0.9.2. We turned on structured_output (JSON mode) and prefix cache to speed up repeated prompts. Our app sometimes issues concurrent generate calls using the same conversation id (we do optimistic UI).

Mike Eng: Noted. Can you share the full curl you used (headers + body) and the request_id? I'll check serving logs. Also did you specify streaming vs non-streaming?

John (Acme): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -H "Idempotency-Key: x-1" -d '{"model":"redwood-14b-rl","structured_output":true,"prompt":"...","conversation_id":"conv-42"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate  (request_id=rq_9a7b). Non-streaming.

Mike Eng: I can reproduce locally in a quick run. Hypothesis: race between the batcher merging KV/prefix cache results and per-request serialization when structured_output is enabled. If two requests for the same conversation hit the batcher/kv merge almost concurrently, the cached prefix tokens can get attached to the wrong response and produce concatenated JSON blobs.

Jen SRE: We already saw a small spike in 5xx for us-west around the deploy window (linked alert). Suggest temporary mitigation: route traffic for customers using structured_output to the older model variant without prefix caching (can flip via routing config) until we patch. Also consider lowering batch window for that traffic.

Luis Infra: I'll try a targeted repro in staging. Quick reproduce script (run N parallel requests):
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 50); do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood-14b-rl","structured_output":true,"conversation_id":"conv-bleed"}' \
  https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done; wait
```
This reliably produced concatenated JSON in my run.

Mike Eng: Workaround for customers: set "prefix_cache": false OR enforce max_concurrency=1 for requests that require strict structured_output. Also enabling streaming parsing on client helps reduce invalid JSON surface.

John (Acme): We flipped prefix_cache off and the invalid JSON stopped immediately. Billing spike also stopped. Thanks. :thumbsup:

Anna Billing: John — can you confirm affected timeframe and invoice/usage id so we can look into token refund? We'll need the window and request ids (rq_9a7b and any others).

Maya - Support: I'll collect the request ids from John and coordinate refunds with Billing.

Mike Eng: Action items: 1) reproduce and add unit/regression test to batcher+kv merge for structured_output (owner: Mike Eng) 2) Add a defensive serialization lock per conversation_id when structured_output=true (owner: Mike Eng) 3) Add a flag to opt out of prefix cache automatically when structured_output=true (owner: Infra) 4) Monitor us-west for related 5xxs (owner: Jen SRE). ETA: tomorrow EOD for tentative fix in staging.

Jen SRE: I'll keep paged monitoring and post any anomalies.

Maya - Support: Thanks all — following up with John on refunds and will keep the customer updated.

DeployBot: deploy "runtime-rev-2026-03-16" was rolled back in us-west at 2026-03-16T23:10:12Z due to elevated 5xxs.

John (Acme): Appreciate the fast triage. Please keep me posted.
